 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that was occurred on 22.05.2022.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 22.05.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-KG-0315 on Doddakoli towards Hampapura on Kodlipete, Sakleshpura, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-MR-2001 coming from opposite side driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and also under gone surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 21 years and was studying in B.Com.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, petitioner is still under treatment and suffered permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. In spite of service of summons, respondent No.1 owner has not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
This respondent has issued a Policy bearing No.OG-22-1701-1825-00001170 in favour of first respondent in respect of Car bearing No.KA-51- MR-2001and it is valid from 16.08.2021 to 15.08.2022.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident and also the involvement of the offending car in the said accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.
4.
On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

As per the spot mahazar and sketch marked at Ex.P3 & 4 the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding.
This shows that the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-51-MR-2001 came to extreme right side/wrong side and caused the accident.
10. The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the motorcycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider has got damages in its front mudguard, front wheel assembly and scratch guard damaged.

Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 22.05.2022 which was caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-MR-2001.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-MR- 2001.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
Petitioner has alleged that at the time of accident he was aged about 21 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P23 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 25.05.2002.
The accident took place on 22.05.2022.
Hence as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 20 years.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P13 the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at KIMS hospital from 30.05.2022 to 02.06.2022 for a period of 4 days and sustained Post Traumatic Left Gallezi Fracture.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/-
may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P17 amounting to Rs.48,639/-.
This bill is supported by the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.48,700/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was a B.Com Student at the time of accident.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 copy of B.com 6th Semester marks card which shows that the petitioner passed his 6th semester of B.com examination of August 2023.
this shows that at the time of accident the petitioner was a student and had no income to hold that he was earning as such loss of income during the laid up period.
No evidence is placed by showing by showing the academic loss to the petitioner.

In the cross-examination of PW1,
the PW1 answered that at the time accident he was studying in the II year B.com and now he has completed his B.com degree.
This shows that there is no academic loss or loss of income during the laid up period.
Hence, no compensation awarded under this head.

5 d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2, through him Clinical notes and X-ray are marked at Ex.P24 and 25.

sentences.text: According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained post trauma fracture of the left radius.
PW.2 was not treated doctor of the petitioner.
Petitioner suffered disability of left arm at 38% and to the whole body at 13%.
According to the petitioner he was a B.com student and suffered with displaced fracture left radius.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his future career to greater extent.

No doubt that at the time of accident the petitioner was not earning, but now he has completed his education and certainly the disability assessed by the PW2 doctor come in to the date to day work of the petitioner.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 11% to the whole body.
No evidence is placed by showing the exact income of the petitioner.
In the absence of evidence the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,500/- per month.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 18 X 11% =Rs.3,68,280/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to KIMS Hospital and took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner admitted to KIMS Hospital as per Ex.P13 and underwent surgery for the fractures sustained by him.
There is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner was in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges of Rs.4,000/- - in total as he was inpatient for a period of 4 days in the hospital as pleaded in the petition.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The fracture of radius has impact on the lifestyle of the petitioner.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 in his affidavit evidence has stated that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by her, I inclined to award Rs.40,000/- under this head.

Liability:-
According to the petitioner, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MR- 2001.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance policy to the offending car bearing No. vehicle bearing No.KA-51-MR-2001.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.

Accordingly,
this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,50,980/- (Rupees Five lakhs fifty thousand nine hundred eighty only) along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the compensation amount awarded, it is ordered to release entire amount in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
